h1: The 6 Best Professional Electric Pruning Shears of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Pro Pruning Shears 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six professional electric pruning shears, from FELCO orchard tools to budget high-capacity models, compared on cut size, safety.
summary: The FELCO 834 is our top pick for full-day orchard and vineyard work. The FELCO 2e is the safer, lighter-duty way into the FELCO line, and the Kebtek 40MM is the near-pro alternative at a lower price. The ANTTCTIG is the budget pick with two batteries and spare blades.
intro: Cutting capacity is the number every listing leads with, and it is the wrong place to start. A professional spends hours a day on the same motion, so hand fatigue, blade quality and finger safety decide whether a shear earns its keep, long before the maximum branch diameter does.

We reviewed six shears on paper, looking at stated cut size, blade coating, battery setup and safety features. The order below follows what each maker claims and what crews report, with nofield trials, and prices are shown as buckets. Two listings, a pole lopper and a thinly described DEWALT, were dropped as poor fits.

products.name: FELCO 834 Electric Pruning Shear, 1.6" Cutting Capacity, Cut Shield & F-Gold Blade for Professional Vineyard, Orchard, Farm Use
products.verdict: The tool built for a full day in the vines.
products.description:
The FELCO 834 offers a 1.6 inch cutting capacity, the Cut Shield safety system and an F-Gold blade, aimed squarely at vineyard, orchard and farm crews. It sits in the $500+ bucket.

It ranks first because it is the only pick marketed for sustained professional use, and it pairs that with finger-detection safety. The FELCO 2e below is cheaper but aimed at lighter work.

Buy it if pruning is your job. The caveat is price, which is hard to justify for a weekend garden.
products.idealFor: Orchard and vineyard professionals pruning all day.
products.skipIf: You prune a few hours per season.

products.name: FELCO 2e Electric Pruning Shears with Cut Shield Safety, F-Tech Coated Blade, 10.8V Lithium Battery
products.verdict: FELCO safety and blades in a lower tier.
products.description:
The FELCO 2e uses a 10.8V lithium battery, an F-Tech coated blade and the Cut Shield safety feature. It falls in the $200-500 bucket.

The silver medal is earned since it brings the same safety idea as the 834 for less, though its listing does not state a cutting capacity. The Kebtek 40MM undercuts it with a stated size.

It suits buyers who want documented finger safety from an established brand. The caveat is that you should confirm the cut size you need before ordering.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed large cut size.

products.name: Kebtek Electric Pruners Cordless Pruning Shear 40MM Professional
products.verdict: A 40mm cut without the FELCO price.
products.description:
The Kebtek 40MM is a cordless electric pruner marketed as professional with a 40mm cut, about 1.6 inches. Its price lands between $200 and $500.

It ranks third because it matches the 834's cut size on paper for less, but the listing names no safety system or blade coating.

It suits buyers who want near-professional capacity on a smaller budget. The caveat is the thin spec sheet.
products.idealFor: Serious users wanting big cuts for less.

products.name: ANTTCTIG Electric Pruning Shears, 2.75'' Cut, 2 Batteries & Spare Blades
products.verdict: The most stated capacity and extras for the least money.
products.description:
The ANTTCTIG lists a 2.75 inch cutting diameter and ships with two batteries and spare blades. It lands in the $50-100 bucket.

Its fourth spot owes to the fact that the stated capacity beats every FELCO, but the figure is the maker's claim and not a pro-tier guarantee. Two batteries are a real edge for long sessions.

It suits buyers who want maximum stated capacity cheaply. The caveat is unproven durability against pro brands.
products.idealFor: Value buyers who need swap-ready batteries.

products.name: SEESII Electric Pruning Shears 4 Modes, 1.8" Cut Electric Pruners Cordless
products.verdict: Four cutting modes for varied branch sizes.
products.description:
The SEESII offers four modes and a 1.8 inch cut in a cordless body. It is priced somewhere from $50 to $100.

It sits mid-pack at fifth, as the ANTTCTIG gives more extras in the same bucket, while this one adds mode control for thinner twigs versus thick wood.

It suits small-scale pros and serious hobbyists. The caveat is that the spec sheet names no battery count.
products.skipIf: You want a bundled spare battery.

products.name: Kebtek 30mm/1.2" Electric Pruning Shears for Garden Care
products.verdict: Light-duty precision cuts, not thick-branch removal.
products.description:
The Kebtek 30mm cuts up to 1.2 inches and is listed for garden care. It falls in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks last because it costs more than the SEESII yet cuts less. It makes sense mainly for precise, thinner pruning.

It suits gardeners doing detail work. The caveat is that its capacity limits it for heavier jobs.

whatMatters.detail: This is the thickest branch the blades can handle, quoted in millimeters or inches. Cutting near the limit strains the motor and dulls blades quickly. Pick a tool rated above your usual branch size.
Systems like FELCO's Cut Shield detect a finger near the blade and stop it. This matters because electric blades close faster than hands react. Look for it by name in the listing.
Coated blades resist sap and rust and glide through wood. Plain blades gum up sooner. Look for a named coating such as F-Gold or F-Tech.
A second battery lets you keep working while one charges. Spare blades extend the tool's life. Check the box contents in the listing.
Pruning is repetitive, so a heavy tool tires your hand. Professional tools focus on balance. Compare listed weights and read owner feedback about hand strain.

cards.label: Safety-equipped
cards.text: FELCO's Cut Shield stops the blade near a finger. The FELCO 834 and FELCO 2e carry it.

cards.label: Value
cards.text: The ANTTCTIG, SEESII and Kebtek models offer capacity for less but name no finger-detection system.

howToChoose.note: Most professionals should default to safety-equipped tools.

cards.text: A proven blade, finger safety and a design meant for thousands of cuts.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Pruning is paid work, where the FELCO 834 pays back in safety and build.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You prune seasonally, where the ANTTCTIG gives two batteries cheaply.

faq.q: Can I use these on thick branches?
faq.a: Only within the stated capacity. Beyond it, switch to a saw or loppers.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying on capacity alone and ignoring safety and fatigue.

faq.q: Is the FELCO 834 worth it over the Kebtek 40MM?
faq.a: For daily professional use, yes, for the safety and blade. For occasional use the Kebtek is enough.
For long days, yes. The ANTTCTIG includes two.

faq.q: How do I maintain the blades?
faq.a: Clean sap after use and keep them dry. Replace blades when cuts get ragged.
Use gloves and keep fingers clear. Models with finger detection add a layer of protection.

finalTake: The FELCO 834 is the right tool for paid, daily pruning. The FELCO 2e brings the safety system for less, and the Kebtek 40MM is the capable value middle. The ANTTCTIG is the budget buy with two batteries. Choose by hours of use, then safety.
